todays_decisions.reasoning: I follow the Market Analyst's risk-off stance. SPY sits 0.02% above its 200-day line, realized vol is 23.1%, and bonds and credit are falling with stocks. I approve P1, selling all of MCO. This is the L8 follow-through I asked for on 11-18. I accept the Skeptic's point that the 'avoided Industrials bucket' reason is the packet artifact L3 warns about, so the approved thesis rests instead on the lost Financials premise, weakening credit and rising long yields, and MCO's higher beta and lower gp_sector_pct than MSCI. The Implicator shows a clean short-term exit, with MCO buy-blocked until about 12-19. I reject P2, the $15 WMT add, for three reasons. XLP's 21-day return is +3.91%, only 0.91 points above the +3% clause that the add's own invalidation and WMT's stored one both cite, and it has been sliding from +8.62% on 11-12. Neither I nor the Proposer can see the print-day gap, so the 'drop it if it opens 5% higher' guard cannot be applied. The add would also reverse the 11-13 trim at about the same price and lift the Staples factor bet to about 18.6%. A buy at a known post-print price with room on the XLP clause can come at a later run. Cash ends near 15.3%, about $33 over the buffer. That breaks the 11-13 commitment to deploy after 11-19, and I am breaking it for specific reasons rather than L4. The regime filter is one ordinary close from turning off. Under L7, VOO's and VTI's RSP clause has tripped (see below), so up to 23.6% of the book may be sold soon. The Market Analyst also asks for small new equity risk, and the only proposed buy fails on its own clause. L2: WMT's 11-19 report is confirmed by the 8-K 2.02 and the guidance-raise headline. Its next date is unverified, and I say so rather than guessing. L7 held-book review: the stop blocks show no price stop tripped. MCO is NEAR (+2.4%) and is being sold. VOO and VTI are NEAR on SPY 730.20, and I re-date their stop to the Market Analyst's 730.02 (the 200-day as of 11-18) under L6. The qualitative clause both of them store, 'RSP's 21-day return turns negative', is now met: the Market Analyst gives RSP 21d -0.20%. Neither the Proposer nor the Skeptic flagged this. I cannot originate a sale, and I will not loosen the clause to avoid the trip. So under L8 and L9 I record the trip in both theses, and the Proposer owes a proposal to sell VOO and VTI together at the next run. That covers 23.6% of equity on one shared condition. The pre-commitment to sell both if the SPY line breaks stands. I take the Market Analyst's breadth counterweight (RSP still 3.56% above its 200-day) as a reason for the exit to be one combined sale, not as a reason to ignore the clause. FAST: its thesis condition 'a marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging' is met. XLI is 4.70% below its 200-day and Industrials is on the avoid list. It is held only by default on its 0.51 beta and 15.5% stop distance, and I restate it as the next sell candidate. I partly disagree with the Proposer's hold verdict here and agree with the Skeptic that a trim proposal is owed. WMT: guidance was raised, so the guidance clause is not met, and XLP 21d +3.91% leaves the XLP clause untripped but close. I restate the stale pre-print text and keep the $119 stop. CARG, DPZ, IDXX, EXEL, MSCI and SAM have no guidance cut or negative 8-K, and all are on the 11-17 menu. The INCY and VRSN insider sales are sentiment, not clause events. KR's cyber clause is unconfirmed, and its 12-03 print is outside the window. MSCI's text is restated as the sole financial-data name after the MCO sale.

trades.thesis: L8 follow-through on the first named sell candidate. The Market Analyst dropped Financials from his favored list on 11-18 and favors only Staples and Utilities today. He reports weakening credit (HYG 1.07% and LQD 2.01% below their 200-day) and rising long yields, which weigh on ratings issuance. Within the MSCI/MCO financial-data sleeve (L3), MCO is the weaker name: beta 0.54 vs 0.37 and gp_sector_pct 0.825 vs 0.903. Selling it halves the sleeve's shared leverage_not_up exposure. The packet's Industrials bucket for MCO is an artifact and is not a reason for this sale. No price stop or stored clause has tripped. The sale realizes a small short-term loss on the single 11-16 lot, and MCO is buy-blocked by the wash-sale window until about 2026-12-19.
trades.invalidation: MCO closes back above $509.04 (its fill) within 20 sessions, or beats SPY over the next 20 sessions.

rejected.why: I accept the Skeptic's serious timing objection.
